{{Short description|none}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2021}} {{use American English|date=July 2021}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania | country = Pennsylvania | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania | next_year = 2024 | seats_for_election = All 17 Pennsylvania seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = November 8, 2022 | party1 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election1 = 9 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election2 = 9 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = }} {{Elections in Pennsylvania}} The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect representatives for the seventeen seats in Pennsylvania (reduced from 18 in the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting cycle]] following the [[2020 United States Census]]). [[Pennsylvania General Assembly|Pennsylvania's legislature]] enacted new district maps in January 2022, which were promptly vetoed by Governor [[Tom Wolf]]. The [[Supreme Court of Pennsylvania|state supreme court]] took control of the process and selected a map in February 2022. After the court rejected several legal challenges in March, the new district boundaries were used in the May 2022 primary elections.{{cite web |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Redistricting_in_Pennsylvania_after_the_2020_census#Apportionment_and_release_of_census_data |title=Redistricting in Pennsylvania after the 2020 census |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=June 5, 2022 }}{{cite news |url=https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2022/03/pennsylvania-legislative-maps-constitutional-supreme-court-challenges/ |title=Pa.
